## Context / Problem
After S2, read/check paths use operation bindings, but live apply, Git push, ACLI/delivery, and bridge orchestration still rebuild config or reuse broad parent environments. Jira Cloud write scope still has the local `DIG` fallback. These paths can write under an unintended scope or leak a Rebar-materialized credential to an unrelated sibling child.

## Outcome
Cut write/apply and subprocess paths over to the S2 runtime. Add one shared child-environment builder: trusted same-capability children start from ambient inheritance, owning children receive their adapter overlay, unrelated siblings remove exact secret names declared by other Rebar adapters, unknown native Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA variables survive, and Rebar never mutates global `os.environ`.

## Plan
1. Thread `ReconcilerSettings`, `GitRuntime`, selected `BridgeRuntime`, and the already-constructed backend through applier, mutation planning/dispatch, inbound/outbound handlers, binding updates, Git adapter/ref/lock/push, and `_bridge_runner` delivery paths. Remove their ambient `load_config`/cwd/default fallbacks.
2. Add `src/rebar/_child_env.py` with a pure environment projection API and a checked-in registry of exact secret names owned by each Rebar adapter. The registry contains names, never values; native SDK/helper chains remain ambient.
3. Ensure CLI `-c` tracker/Jira/reconciler selections cross the reconciler subprocess boundary as non-secret snapshot material. Pass static adapter material only to the exact owning process/adapter.
4. Remove the Jira Cloud write-side `DIG` fallback. Missing explicit write scope fails before mutation. Preserve existing retry, rate-limit, TLS, output, partial-failure, idempotency, and ticket-delivery behavior unless a test names the approved delta.

## Testing (RED -> GREEN)
- End-to-end verified-fake Cloud/DC runs cover create/update/comment/link/delete/inbound apply plus Git commit/push/delivery under custom tracker dir/branch/remote with ambient resolvers poisoned after composition.
- Child-process contract tests assert unknown ambient/native-chain variables survive; the owning overlay appears only for its child; unrelated siblings lose other adapters' exact declared names; argv/URL/log/output contain no secret sentinel.
- Concurrency tests run distinct operations with different overlays and timeouts, asserting `os.environ` is byte-equal before/during/after and no cross-operation value is observed.
- Failure-injection tests cover missing project/auth, revoked credential, TLS error, retry/rate-limit exhaustion, provider partial failure, and delivery failure; existing provider-neutral output and recovery/idempotency oracles remain authoritative.
- A red test demonstrates the current `DIG` fallback; green asserts zero provider mutation when write scope is absent.

## Compatibility / rollback
Until bounded-live validation, a compatibility facade may invoke the legacy write path. Before cutover, rollback selects it. After any new snapshot-aware caller ships, rollback requires the S1 envelope-compatible floor. Ticket, event, bridge, and binding formats remain unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Verified-fake Cloud/DC apply plus Git/delivery paths complete with ambient resolvers poisoned and use the configured tracker directory/branch/remote and explicit project scope.
- [ ] Missing Cloud write scope produces a typed/redacted pre-mutation failure and no request uses `DIG` unless `DIG` was explicitly configured.
- [ ] Same-capability child tests preserve unknown Git/SSH/AWS/proxy/CA variables, owning children receive only their overlay, and unrelated siblings omit every other adapter's exact declared secret name.
- [ ] Concurrent-operation tests prove no global environment mutation and no cross-operation credential/config observation.
- [ ] Existing retry, rate-limit, TLS, output, partial-failure, recovery, and idempotency scenarios retain their provider-neutral behavior except explicitly approved deltas.
- [ ] Disabling the write facade restores the legacy path before cutover; no stored ticket/event/bridge/binding format changes.
